newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Aeroflot takes fresh look at Shannon hub.
newsitem.headline: Aeroflot takes fresh look at Shannon hub.

text.p: Russian international flag carrier Aeroflot wants to improve the efficiency of its use of a hub at Ireland's Shannon airport, a senior company official said.
Aeroflot deputy chief executive Valery Okulov told Reuters that flights between Shannon and U.S. destinations were only profitable from June to September.
"In others seasons we make losses," he said.
Okulov said that operation of outdated Ilyushin Il-62s on routes from Shannon was not efficient.
"We plan to replace this type of aircraft soon, making our operations there more profitable," he added.
Aeroflot began to use Shannon as a hub in May last year, operating Il-62s for regular flights to New York and Chicago and charters to Nassau, Bahamas, Mexico, Havana, Santiago, Lima and Barbados.
Smaller CIS airlines, which lack long-haul fleets, fly from various points in the former Soviet Union to Shannon and transfer their passengers to Aeroflot there.
Okulov said Aeroflot did not plan to stop operations from Shannon.
"Small airlines from Russia, Moldova, Belarus and Ukraine have a big interest in linking up to the (Shannon) wayport," Okulov said.
The Irish airport was offering low service rates, landing fees and cheap hotel rates for Aeroflot crew and passengers in Shannon.
In the Soviet era, Aeroflot used Shannon for re-fuelling on transatlantic flights, but later began non-stop flights across the Atlantic from Russia.
